stem.en: A pesticide company proposes a synthetic ant pheromone that lasts for months, "so a single application controls ants all season". Kabir thinks it is clever. What does the sim predict?

text.en: Ants would follow it to wherever it was laid, for months, whatever was there. It could lure them into traps for a while, but it would also jam their own trails and, more likely, the colony would learn to ignore that molecule, since a constant smell carries no news.

feedback.en: A permanent trail is noise. Real trails work because they change.

text.en: Ants would starve, so it is a good pesticide.

feedback.en: Perhaps briefly. Colonies adapt to constant signals by ceasing to respond, from III.6's idea of equilibrium applied to behaviour.
Long-lasting versions of pheromones are made routinely. The problem is what a permanent signal means, not whether it can exist.

explanation.en: A message's value is in its change. A signal that never changes is quickly treated as background.
